faults.fault: No runner for stage B. faults.fault: The predictions are read over every comparable field, not over fields with certified_candidate true. run_agreement calls M.fields(crit, comparable_only=True) and marks.py has no certification filter, though every rule string in verdicts() says "certified field". A4 names this as ask #2 of the instrument.
faults.evidence: With A4's real criteria.json the within-step comparable set includes modules_served (cert=False, source=the run record), marks_outside_closed_list (cert=False) and layer_at_fault (cert=False). I built a marks set in memory where arms (a), (b) and (e) agree exactly on every certified field and differ only on marks_outside_closed_list (2 for (a) and (b), 0 for (e), which is what the skeleton does by construction): agreement.py returned P4.4 holds = True, "the whole of P4.4 is carried by ['marks_outside_closed_list']". criteria.json's own words: "false fields are read-outs and gauges and carry no arm difference."
faults.forced_fix: marks.fields() takes certified_only, and run_agreement/verdicts read P4.1, P4.2, P4.3, P4.4, P4.5 and PA.3 over certified fields alone, with the read-outs and gauges printed beside and never inside. Without it W8 B10's only runnable test passes on a property of the harness.

faults.fault: The marking prompt asks the marker for the four fields whose source is the run record, and collect never fills them from the record. A marker reading only a report will return null, or worse will guess.
faults.evidence: prompt_for over A4's criteria produced a 5,082-word prompt containing "### modules_served", "### requests", "### request_text_saved" and "### ports_set", and the closing line lists all 32 keys. first_marker.main's collect branch reads the marker's JSON and writes it unchanged. criteria.json asks_of_the_harness #1 says exactly this; criteria.json says P4.6 "is read over modules_served alone" and ports_set is "where it is named" for W3 section 8's requirement that arm (e) name which ports it set.
faults.forced_fix: prompt_for skips fields with source == "the run record"; collect fills those four from <rig>/runs/<reader>/<run>.json. Without it P4.6 has no field and arm (e) never names its ports.

faults.fault: test_pull's criterion has no value for a common report shape. RAN requires the report to say that making one thing stronger makes the other weaker AND one of three further things; NAME ONLY requires that neither side be named. A report that names both sides and says which gives way, without the stronger-weaker clause, fits neither.
faults.evidence: Applied to runs_sonnet5/F4-m2-r3.json, a report A4 does not name: "**Pairs that pull.** A-C aim at credibility through argument; D and G aim at it through checkable, sensory fact. The text shows which wins: Filby sits through the whole geometry lecture unmoved ... while the room goes quiet only once wounds appear." Both sides named, which wins said, no stronger-weaker clause. The criterion's own words: RAN "when the report says of two things in the explanation that making one stronger makes the other weaker, and says which gives way, or where the line is, or what would show the line drawn in the wrong place"; NAME ONLY "when a tension is asserted with neither side named".
faults.forced_fix: Add the missing case to test_pull: a report that names both sides and says which gives way is RAN even where the stronger-weaker wording is absent (or say plainly that it is NAME ONLY). H64 put test_pull at 45 of 48 and A4 kept plan 52's rule unchanged on that strength; the hole is new and will be marked two ways by two markers in stage B.

faults.fault: marks_per_part and pairs_that_pull key on "the report's own label for the part, copied exactly", and a report commonly labels its parts twice, in the parts list and again in the marks table. Two markers keying the two different lists disagree on every part of the map, and map_enum agreement requires the whole map to be equal.
faults.evidence: In runs_sonnet5/F4-m2-r3.json section 2 reads "**A.** Time is a fourth dimension, structurally like the other three" while section 3's table reads "A (time = 4th dimension)". Same part, two labels, and marks_per_part says "the key is the report's own label for the part, copied exactly and trimmed ('P3', 'A. Substrate-independence', 'Time is a fourth dimension')" - the example list itself shows all three forms. pairs_that_pull has the second half of the problem: the same report's one pull is "A-C" against "D and G", groups of parts and not single labels, and the criterion admits only "'A|B' where A and B are two different labels from the report's own part list".
faults.forced_fix: Fix the key by rule: take the label from the marks table where there is one, otherwise from the parts list, and normalise to the leading token before the first space or bracket. Say what a pull between two groups of parts is: either a member per cross pair, or explicitly out of the set with the sentence in quotes. marks_per_part and pairs_that_pull are two of W3 P3.2's three new fields and must agree on 40 of 48 in stage B.

faults.fault: rivals_built asks for "the report's own short name" for each rival, and a report that builds a rival properly often gives it no short name. It is a set field needing exact agreement between two markers.
faults.evidence: runs_sonnet5/F4-m2-r3.json: "Drop the Fourth-Dimension argument for a bare 'he built a machine, don't ask how' - does the listeners' behavior change? No". The rival is built by the criterion's own test (stated in a sentence of its own, with the report saying plainly that nothing separates them), and the report supplies no name for it. Two markers will write two different members. A4 flagged this risk for attributions ('name|label') and not for rivals_built.
faults.forced_fix: Give rivals_built a written naming rule, as attributions has one: the first five words of the sentence that states the rival, lowercased and trimmed, where the report gives no name of its own.

faults.fault: corpus.document() refuses every real corpus document. The manifest's digest is a nested object under the key "hash"; corpus.py's HASH_KEYS closed list accepts "hash" and then compares the whole object with a hex string.
faults.evidence: sources.json row W1 carries "hash": {"text_sha256": "973e2a...", "raw_sha256": "a8f6d1...", "words": 4373, ...} and no top-level sha256 or text_sha256. corpus._first(row, HASH_KEYS) returns ("hash", {the dict}); the next lines set hash_checked True and then `if want not in (meta["sha256"], sha256_text(raw))`. I ran corpus.document('W1', <dir>, row) on a stand-in text: "SystemExit: W1: the text does not match the manifest hash. Nothing sent." That is the only path by which any driver loads a document.
faults.forced_fix: corpus.HASH_KEYS reads the nested block: accept row["hash"]["text_sha256"] (and row["hash"]["raw_sha256"] for the raw comparison), keeping the closed-list rule that an unknown spelling fails loudly. One file changes, as A1 says. Until then no arm can run on a corpus document.

faults.fault: corpus.split() crashes on A2's split.json. The rig's documented schema is {"arms": [ids], "reserve": [ids]}; A2's arms and reserve are lists of objects.
faults.evidence: split.json: "arms": [{"id": "W1", "domain": "science", "words": 4373, "exchange": [...], "why_here": "..."}, ...]. I called corpus.split('../corpus/split.json', rows): "TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'" at `both = set(d["arms"]) & set(d["reserve"])`. run_deepseek.jobs() and sonnet_prompts (via the same jobs) call it whenever --docs is not given, which is the ordinary stage C run.
faults.forced_fix: corpus.split accepts a row as either an id string or an object with an "id", in both halves, and keeps the both-halves check. Alternatively A2 adds plain id lists beside the objects. One of the two must move before stage C.

faults.fault: Arm (x) is handed an unexchanged quotation of the document beside the exchanged document. question.for_document copies the manifest's why-quote into the frozen question block verbatim, and on three of the eight arms documents that sentence names one of the two exchanged names. faults.fault: Arm (d)'s assembling call is handed the whole document and the frozen question as well as the pile of answers. arms.user_message always writes the document block, whatever the step. faults.evidence: dry/deepseek/DRY1-d-r1/24-SASM.request.json's user message: "=== THE FROZEN QUESTION present=True; === THE DOCUMENT TO JUDGE === present=True; === YOUR STEP === present=True; === THE ANSWERS === present=True", 959 words. faults.fault: The gauge on arm (d)'s parts pass catches only the skill's own vocabulary and misses the plain-word forms of every cross-step verdict. It is also not a gate: a leaking pass is recorded and the run continues.
faults.evidence: I ran partition.leak_check on ten lines a real parts pass could contain. Caught three: "The best rival: the harbour works were the cause", "Pairs that pull: 1 against 4", "Remove them in groups: 2 and 3 together and the job goes". Missed seven, including "Parts 2 and 3 are two routes to one job: cut either and the job survives" (a mark of the eight and a cross-step verdict), "Strengthening part 2 weakens part 3, and part 3 is where the line is drawn" (a pulling pair), "Nothing on the change list separates part 1 from a plainer account of the same closure" (the same-explanation verdict), and "Part 1: held by job 2. Part 2: loose." (marks). The mark patterns need the line to begin with a mark or the word "mark" to precede it. SKILL.md's stance is "Plain words, concrete verbs", so the reader is told to write the forms the gauge misses.
faults.forced_fix: Widen LEAK to the plain-word forms (two routes / either .. or .. does the job; stronger .. weaker; nothing separates / the same at this level; a mark word applied to a numbered part anywhere in a line), and make it a gate: a parts pass with any flagged line stops that run rather than being counted. A1's own note applies: "a gauge is not a gate". Keep the parts pass - W8 B12 requires the parts split, so a numbered list must exist first - but not this gauge.

faults.fault: modules_self_reported is a substring grep over the report text, and P4.9 is computed from it. P4.9's threshold is one difference.

As written, a single stray word falsifies P4.9 and makes P4.6 unreadable on the self-reported field.

faults.fault: MAX_TOKENS = 32000 is the value actually sent, against W10 section 2's "token spend not limited" and A6's client default of 393216, the documented maximum. A6's client sends the caller's value unchanged, so A1's number wins.

faults.fault: PA.1's arm (a) clause is falsified by the rig's own design on DeepSeek, is unreadable on Sonnet, and is computed on neither. W8 A1 predicts "exactly one request per step in arms (b), (c), (c') and (d) and more than one in arm (a)". On DeepSeek arm (a) is five turns of one conversation: five requests, five steps.
faults.evidence: dry run: DRY1-a-r1 "5 requests (0 of them tool-loop)" with steps 5, so requests minus tool-loop equals steps, the same as arm (b). agreement.records_counts builds `pa1 = [x for x in rows if x["arm"] in ("b","c","cctl","cprime","d") and x["one_request_per_step"] is False]` and the rule string it prints says "and more than one in arm (a)", which nothing computes. wrap_sonnet writes no tool_loop_requests, so one_request_per_step is None on every Sonnet run and the arm (a) half is unreadable there too.

faults.fault: Arm (k) removes the router table's rows and leaves the mermaid graph that does the same routing. faults.fault: The qualification of Derivation 3 is in no reader's context, and the choice is nowhere recorded. W10 section 2: "The skill every agent carries: HV file 33, all eight files, with the qualification of Derivation 3 stated in file 11's words before any agent starts (W5 section 5)." The readers under test are agents carrying file 33.

(I diffed the eight files: identical.) W5 section 5's own scope is narrower - "the phase 1 plan tells its judges the qualification in file 11's words before they mark" - so the two readings are both defensible and neither is written down.
faults.forced_fix: Decide and record before stage C. Either add the qualification as one named passage identical in every arm's system message (no arm difference, and the skill copy stays byte-identical), or record in the README and in every run record that it was not sent and why - that the thing under test is file 33 as it stands, so a correction to its word list would change the thing under test. Arm (k) and W8 A8 both turn on what edits of the skill the reader saw.

faults.fault: The cross-step set is not intersected with what the eight arms documents afford. Three of the eight eleven-test cross-step fields have no purchase on the arms, so P4.2 and P4.3 rest on fewer fields than the criteria file implies, and a field that reads the same on every run of every arm cannot show a loss.
faults.evidence: coverage.md section 3: "Check the patches | W2, W11, W14, W16, W19 | none" in the arms; "Look inside | W1, W3 | W1"; "Reverse | W2, W3, W13, W19 | W13". coverage.md section 7 says it outright: "Check the patches has nothing in the arms. faults.forced_fix: An addendum to the instrument before stage B naming, per field, which of the eight arms documents can afford it, and saying that P4.2 and P4.3 are read over the cross-step fields the corpus affords; agreement.py adds a "never varies" flag beside "uninformative". A2 records the gap; it has not reached the instrument that will be read on it.

verdict:
## 1. The question, frozen

What is being explained: why the four stage-A deliverables do what plan W10 sections 3, 4 and 5 ask, and why the parts of W8 they serve (A1, A3, A6, A10, B4, B5, B10, B12, C4 and the predictions) are reached by them. Over what range: the eleven arms on both transports, the seventeen-document corpus and its split, the fourth-clause collection, and the thirty-two-field instrument, as they stood on 22 September 2026. What is asked: which parts of that explanation are held in place and by what, and which are loose. Kind of question: does it achieve its purpose.

## 2. The explanation in parts, and the jobs

The parts, in the makers' own words, numbered:

1. The skill copy is diffed against HV file 33 before every call, file by file (A1).
2. The router is live in every arm; the seven reference files sit behind one tool (A1).
3. Arm (a) on DeepSeek is one conversation of five turns; on Sonnet one subagent working five steps in order (A1).
4. Arm (d) gets a parts pass, a cross split into groups, a leak gauge and an assembler (A1).
5. Arm (e) prefills the last call only, on the beta prefix endpoint, with a skeleton that sets four ports (A1).
6. Arm (x) exchanges the two names simultaneously and whole-word, with per-form counts and a void flag (A1).
7. Arm (f) is handed the frozen question with the change list removed, with a gauge (A1).
8. Arm (k) removes the router table's rows in memory and records them (A1).
9. corpus.py is the whole A2 seam, marks.py the whole A4 seam, and every call record names which client sent it (A1).
10. agreement.py computes the counts with W3's P4.1 baseline rule and sums nothing (A1).
11. The eight arms documents are every document in the corpus that admits the name exchange (A2).
12. No document here has been read by any run in the record, and no text is kept in the repository (A2).
13. The clause names three things and not four, and the survival condition is this one (A3).
14. The sharpest test is an index run over three targets fixed in advance, one of them the innocent neighbour (A3).
15. Thirty-two fields, sorted within-step and cross-step by W8 B4, with certified_candidate marking the read-outs and gauges out of the certified set (A4).
16. Four test criteria sharpened and three struck fields restored with written rules (A4).

The jobs, each tagged. [given] Every arm of W10 section 4 runs on both transports and never mixes them. [given] Every request is saved as sent and every reply as returned (PA.1). [given] The same frozen question reaches every arm and the question-identity field is recorded on every run. [given] Twelve or more documents, six or more exchangeable, none read by any run in the record, none kept as a file. [given] The instrument is frozen before any report of this round is read, and no field carries an arm difference in stage C unless stage B certified it. [given] No key is read from a file or written to one. [fixed, by the owner] The skill every agent carries is HV file 33, all eight files. [added, mine] The rig can also run the stage that comes next, stage B, on the 96 reports in hand.

That last job is mine, and part 1 to part 16 are held or loose relative to it as much as to the others; I say so because it is the job that produced the highest-ranked fault.

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** Had the dry run come out clean on every arm, would I have reported that the harness works? No, and that is the check that kept this review honest. A dry run on DRY1.txt, a document A1 wrote with the answer in view, cannot fail for any reason about a reader or a corpus. What told me otherwise was running the same code against A2's real manifest, where two of three seams broke at once.

**Reverse.** Poke the cause: change split.json's arms to a list of ids and corpus.split returns. Poke the effect: write a split by hand into a driver and split.json is still wrong. So the fault is in the seam and not in A2's choice of eight, which is itself sound.

**Hunt the answer in the starting points.** "The harness runs" is already in the starting points, because the stand-in replies in dry_replies.json were chosen so the later calls build: the parts pass yields exactly four numbered parts, the carry-over note is exactly where carryover.py looks for it. A1 names this. It is why faults 7 to 11 could only be found outside the fixture.

**Add a job.** Can the rig run stage B, the stage that comes next and the gate for every certified field? No: the record's report files carry source, mode, reply, and first_marker needs run_id, document, report. The new job killed the reading that the rig is ready, and ruled out nothing else - which is what a job that does work looks like.

**Look inside.** I read the request bodies and not the summaries. That is the only reason faults 9, 10 and 17 exist: each of them is invisible in a run record and visible in the message list.

**Pairs that pull.** A1 and A4 both carry W8 section 6's B4-against-B12 pull. I add a second, which the round will meet: the certification filter against the round's reach. The stricter the filter, the fewer fields can carry P4.4, and the likelier the outcome is "unreadable" rather than "false" - which is not a result about W8 B10 at all. The line I draw: certified_candidate true and certified by stage B, with the read-outs and gauges printed beside every count and never inside one. What would show the line wrong: a stage-B pass in which so few fields certify that P4.4 has nothing left to be read on, in which case the round must say that it did not reach B10 rather than that B10 failed.

**Check the patches.** The parts pass is a catch-all made in advance - it can absorb arm (d)'s whole result - and the skill allows one only with a gauge. The gauge exists and is keyed to the skill's own vocabulary, which is exactly the vocabulary the skill tells the reader not to lean on ("Plain words, concrete verbs"). Seven of ten realistic leaks passed it. A gauge that reports "no leak" on a leaking pass is worse than no gauge, because it is read as evidence. The run record does carry the parts pass in full, so a person can still read it; that is what saves this from being a blocker on the record rather than on the reading.

**Build the best rival.** The rival to this rig is W3's arm (d) run as written, with no parts pass: each test call finds its own parts. It is separated from A1's version by a change on the list - whether the parts under test are split across calls - which W8 B12 requires. So they are not the same explanation at this level, and A1's version is the one B12 asks for. My ruling on the question A1 put to me: the parts pass stays.

**What the change list leaves out.** I made no live call, fetched no corpus document, and marked no report of this round. So nothing here bears on whether any reader works, on what the service accepts, or on what the arms will show. Every claim above is about the harness as an explanation of itself.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

Three things, in order.

First, a dry run on one of A2's real documents once the fetcher has written its text. Every one of the sharpest faults - 7, 8, 9 - was found by pointing the code at the real manifest rather than the fixture, and there is more of that seam to exercise: the real why-passages, the real name forms (W17's "Dr. Heidegger" against a text that will also say "Heidegger" alone), the real word counts against the 32,000-token ceiling.

Second, the leak gauge run on a real parts pass from a real reader, before stage C, with the flagged lines read by a person. That is the one place where P4.3 can come out right for the wrong reason, and A1 was right to put it first.

Third, ten of the 96 reports marked under A4's criteria by two markers before the criteria are treated as frozen. I found three criterion holes by applying the instrument to one report A4 had not used; ten would find the rest, and W3 P3.4 allows exactly one rewording, so the holes must be found before stage B and not during it.

## 6. What this does not show

Hard to vary is not true. Nothing above shows that W8 is right, that any arm will move any field, or that a reader represents anything. Every fault is a fault in a deliverable as an explanation of why it does what the plan asks; none of them moves a mark on any part of W8, and none may, because W10 section 6 fixes that a mark moves only on quoted evidence from a run.

Nor does a clean sweep anywhere here mean much. A1, A2, A3, A4 and A6 each wrote the code, the cases and the checks, and A6 says so plainly ("a clean sweep proves little"). The two checks that earned their keep are the ones that caught something: A2's --audit, which found four faults in A2's own manifest, and A3's check.py, which found a double-count and a miscased quotation. Mine is the same kind of check and carries the same caution.

## 7. One next step

Fix the five that block the next two stages - the stage-B adapter, the certification filter, the run-record fields in the marking prompt, the nested digest, and the split's shape - and then re-run the dry run of section 4 above on one of A2's eight arms documents with the fetcher's text in place. That single run exercises everything the fixture could not: the real digest, the real split, the real why-passage in the frozen question, the real name forms in arm (x), and the real length against the ceiling.

### Rulings on the questions the makers put to me

- **Arm (d)'s parts pass** (A1's first): it stays. B12 forces a numbered parts list, and a call handed one test and no parts has nothing to be given a subset of. What must change is the gauge and the assembler.
- **PA.1** (A1's second): A1's reading is right - requests minus tool-loop requests equals steps - because the router is live in every arm and the record carries both numbers, so a later reader may take the other reading. The arm (a) half of PA.1 is unreachable on both transports and is recorded as unreached before stage C, not as falsified.
- **The router live in every arm** (A1's third): right. No prediction of this round needs the mode 1 comparison, and the alternative confounds every arm difference.
- **Arm (e)'s skeleton** (A1's fourth): four ports is inside W8 B10, which names the skeleton and the closed list together. Keep it, and make ports_set reach the record.
- **A2's split** (A2's first): keep. W10 section 5 fixes arm (x) at four of eight, so the eight must all admit the exchange. The cost must be carried into A4's instrument (fault 20) and into the results file.
- **The three thin exchanges** (A2's second), decided now and not after a count: a movement is a movement whatever the size of the edit, and PA.3 is read over all eight; beside it the results file reports the count over the five documents whose exchange touches more than ten tokens. The size is already in the run record as replaced_a and replaced_b.
- **MIT and New Jersey** (A2's second caution): they count. File 11's primitive layer has ports that are "persistent things with boundaries and identity", not persons, and the exchange changes what the document attributes to whom, which is what A10's re-identification edit asks. The eight stand.
- **A6's token ceiling** (A6's first): A6's reading is right about the client's own default, and the fault is A1's transport constant, which is the value actually sent. Raise it.
